title: Min Cost to Connect Points
statement:
Lay cable between points on a plane so that every point is connected to every other, as cheaply as possible.

Contract
- `points[i] = {x, y}` with integer coordinates. A cable between two points costs their Manhattan distance, `|x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|`.
- Cables may only join two given points, but the network may pass through any point, so connectivity is transitive.
- Return the smallest total cost that links all points. Zero or one point costs 0; duplicate points are allowed and cost 0 to join.
- The total always fits in an `int`. Do not modify `points`.

Examples
- `{{0,0},{2,2},{3,10},{5,2},{7,0}}` returns `20`.
- `{{4,4}}` returns `0`.
- `{{1,1},{4,5}}` returns `7`.
hints: Treat the points as a complete graph with Manhattan-distance edge weights. Cheapest connection of everything is a minimum spanning tree.

Always growing from the already-connected set by its cheapest outgoing cable is correct (Prim). Always hopping to the nearest unvisited point from where you stand is not, because it can leave a cheap link behind.

Keep, for every unconnected point, its cheapest distance to the connected set; repeatedly attach the minimum and refresh the others. Intended complexity: O(n^2) time with no explicit edge list and O(n) space (Kruskal would need O(n^2 log n) over all edges).
inputSyntax: Input: points as x,y pairs separated by spaces, for example: 0,0 2,2 3,10 5,2 7,0
